title: ACL List 0.2 — payload
description: Enumerate the AclEntry 0.2 records a maintainer holds, with optional conjunctive filters and paging. A hierarchical filter (`context`, `resource`) MUST state its `direction`; there is no default direction. The outer document members are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

role.description: Optional filter — only entries with this role are returned.

context.description: Optional filter on the entries' ACT scope, read in the stated `direction`. REQUIRES `direction`. Replaces 0.1's `scope` filter.

capability.description: Optional filter — only entries whose EFFECTIVE capability set includes this capability (the role's full ceiling for `capabilities: {scope: ceiling}`, nothing for `none`, and for `listed` the ceiling ∩ the non-additive grants plus the additive grants). Combined with `resource`, the capability must be held at a qualifier related to that resource by `direction`.

resource.description: Optional filter on the resource qualifiers of the entries' effective capabilities (of `capability` when given, of any capability otherwise), read in the stated `direction`. REQUIRES `direction`.

direction.description: How to read a hierarchical filter (`context`, `resource`). REQUIRED when either is present and REFUSED when neither is: `actingIn` — entries whose scope or qualifier is an ancestor-or-self of the queried one, i.e. who may act IN it (unrestricted act scopes and unqualified capabilities match); `subtree` — entries holding a grant at or BENEATH the queried one (an unrestricted act scope or an unqualified capability does NOT match, and an entry naming contexts both inside and outside the subtree DOES); `any` — the union. Same three questions as 0.1's `acting-in` / `subtree` / `any`, re-cased to lowerCamelCase, with no default.

subjectPrefix.description: Optional filter — only entries whose subject VID starts with this prefix are returned.

pageSize.description: Maximum number of entries to return. Maintainer-defined default and ceiling.

cursor.description: Opaque continuation token returned by the maintainer in a previous response. It binds the filters and `direction` it was minted under; a follow-up request MUST repeat them unchanged.

Response.title: ACL List 0.2 — response payload
Response.description: The success response to an acl/list/0.2 request. Carried in a Trust Task document whose type is https://trusttasks.org/spec/acl/list/0.2#response.

entries.description: Matching AclEntry items, in maintainer-defined order. May be empty.

truncated.description: true when more matching entries exist beyond `entries`; false when this response is the complete result. Independent of `cursor`: a maintainer MAY truncate without supporting pagination, in which case `truncated` is true and `cursor` is absent.

cursor.description: Opaque continuation token to fetch the next page. Present only when `truncated` is true AND the maintainer supports pagination from this point. Binds the request's filters and direction. Consumers MUST treat it as opaque and re-send it verbatim.

redactedFields.description: Names of AclEntry members the maintainer redacted from every returned entry. `act`, `keys` and `capabilities` are never redacted; `approve` and `approveCapabilities` SHOULD NOT be (see acl/show/0.2).
